learning_objective: 🎯 Analyze a satirical play that highlights the unpaid, taken-for-granted labor of housewives and the drastic measures needed to earn respect in the family!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Mrs. Annie Pearson is a loving, submissive housewife who works 24/7 without a word of thanks. Her husband (George) and children (Doris and Cyril) treat her like a servant.
Her bold, smoking, fortune-telling neighbor, Mrs. Fitzgerald, offers a solution. Using magic she learned in the East, they swap personalities. Mrs. Fitzgerald's tough soul enters Mrs. Pearson's body.
The 'new' Mrs. Pearson shocks the family. She smokes, drinks stout, refuses to make tea, refuses to iron clothes, and mocks Doris's boyfriend and George's club friends.
Doris cries, Cyril is confused, and George is humiliated. For the first time, they realize how helpless they are without the mother they always ignored.
Once the family is humbled, the women swap back to their original bodies. The family now treats Mrs. Pearson with respect, deciding to stay home and play a game of rummy with her.

fun_activity.title: 🎭 Personality Swap Roleplay
fun_activity.instructions: Imagine swapping personalities with your strictest teacher. How would you talk to your friends? Now imagine your teacher acting like you! Write down one funny dialogue of this swap.

exam_tips: 📌 Contrast the characters of Mrs. Pearson (timid, loving) and Mrs. Fitzgerald (bold, aggressive).
📌 Understand the central theme: The unpaid and unappreciated labor of housewives in a patriarchal setup.
📌 Detail how the 'new' Mrs. Pearson tackled George, Doris, and Cyril individually.
quick_recap: ⭐ 'Mother's Day' is a comedic play with a serious social message.
⭐ The club members call George 'Pompy-ompy Pearson' behind his back because he is slow and pompous.
⭐ The play ends with a warning from Mrs. Fitzgerald: don't go soft on them again!
